problems: The quote is real. It is the Info cell of the ES-1 row in Table 9 on PDF p.63: 'Engineering Soil 1 - ESA TN-MMA-MVW-20140606'. But that text is the identifier of an ESA technical note, not a release or production year for the simulant. Neither document gives a release date. The year 2014 is inferred from the '20140606' part of the code, as the extractor admits.
The ESRIC page (NEW1) has no date and no TN code at all. It only says 'Previously produced, some stockpiles exist, may be difficult to reproduce if needed'.
Should be recorded as unsupported, or at most as 'inferred from ESA document code' if the curator accepts that standard. It must not get a superscript that implies ISECG states a 2014 release.
Agreed that 'Unavailable' is not stated anywhere. ISECG Table 9, ES-1 row, Contact Info/Comments cell (p.63): 'Unknown availability. May be obtained from RUAG.'

The rendered p.63 shows the ES-1 Supply Confidence cell in amber. The table key defines amber as '= Previously produced, some stockpiles exist, may be difficult to reproduce if needed'. The ESRIC ES-1 entry gives the same wording in its Availability field.
'Unavailable' is not one of the allowed values in data-schema.md ('Available', 'Limited Stock', 'Production stopped', 'Unknown'). The sources point to 'Unknown' (ISECG) or 'Limited Stock' (ESRIC).

The quote exists (p.63, Info cell), but 'Engineering Soil' there is just the expansion of the product name 'ES-1'. data-schema.md defines lunar_sample_reference as 'What lunar sample it replicates'. Neither document says ES-1 replicates any lunar sample.

Both documents file ES-1 as a Mars simulant. In ISECG Table 9 it sits under an orange 'Mars' sub-heading in the ESA block. On the ESRIC page it is under 'Mars Regolith Simulants'. The quote does not support this field; it should be unsupported, or the field cleared.
Agreed that 'Open University' is unsupported. The ESRIC ES-1 entry says 'Supplier/Contact RUAG Space United Kingdom'. ISECG p.63, ES-1 row: 'May be obtained from RUAG.', inside the ESA block.
Open University appears only in the next rows of both sources: 'OUCM-1 and CM-2 Open University', OUEB/QUEB-1, OUHR-1 and OUSR-1.

checks.notes: Checked PDF p.63 (of 124) with pdftotext and by rendering the page at 150 dpi. The ES-1 row reads: Info 'Engineering Soil 1 - ESA TN-MMA-MVW-20140606' | Type 'Fine dust (Nepheline Syenite) from Sibelco, Norway. Large volume, mechanical.' | Contact Info/Comments 'Unknown availability. May be obtained from RUAG.' | Supply Confidence amber. The extractor's mention quote runs these cells together in order and is accurate. The NEW1 quote matches the ESRIC page's consecutive fields in order (Name / ES-1 / Description / ... / Supplier/Contact / RUAG Space / United Kingdom). The page title is 'ESRIC KSP - Simulants', saved with SingleFile from http://knowledge.esric.lu/simulants/ on 2025-03-03. The ESRIC page does not contain 'Engineering Soil' or the TN code, so it supports neither release_date nor lunar_sample_reference. The extractor's claim that both documents trace back to TN-MMA-MVW-20140606 is not shown by the ESRIC page itself; it cites no source. Library sweep: grep -rliw for ES-1, ES1, 'Engineering Soil', 'Nepheline Syenite', 'Silverbond', 'OMR Dry' and 'TN-MMA' across Sources_text returned only these two files. A search of the text-like files (csv/json/txt/md/html) in the Sources tree for 'Engineering Soil' and 'TN-MMA-MVW' found nothing else. No primary source for ES-1 exists in the library. Both sources class ES-1 as a Mars simulant, so the curator should decide whether it belongs in the lunar database at all.

new_references.title: Properties of novel LX lunar regolith simulant system — the base simulants: Part 2
new_references.authors: Patzwald, J., Kleba-Ehrhardt, R., Griemsmann, T., Nowaczyk, N., Linke, S., Overmeyer, L., Stoll, E., Karl, D.
new_references.mention_quote: The highest AP-cohesive strength was found for LX-T100 with 257.2 Pa, followed by LX-I50 with 214.3 Pa and LX-M100 with 185.2 Pa.

values.note: This is an AVERAGE friction angle across all three LX base simulants (LX-T100, LX-M100, LX-I50) at void ratio e0=0.7/depth 0-30cm, not an individually measured value for LX-M100 alone: 'the average friction angles were calculated from the three simulants sharing the same initial void ratio in each case' (p.10). Individual per-simulant friction angles are only shown graphically in Figs. 10-11, not tabulated numerically.
Table header: 'LX-T100 D50 [μm] | LX-M100 D50 [μm]'; dry-sieving row gives LX-M100=63.7.

values.quote: the base simulants LX-T100 and LX-M100 were separated into particle sizes <45 μm, 45–71 μm, 71–90 μm, 90–125 μm, 125–160 μm, 160–250 μm, 250–500 μm, 500–1000 μm and 1000–2000 μm using wet sieving.

values.note: No explicit 'release date' is stated for the product. 2025 is inferable only from the journal publication metadata (received 20 June 2024, accepted 18 Feb 2025, available online 28 Feb 2025), not from a direct textual claim about the simulant's release.

values.quote: Large quantities of the LX base simulants are available and can already be supplied to research and industry. They are distributed to research partners and can further be purchased commercially by anyone upon request.
The basalt, in turn, represents the regolith of the mare regions and is denoted by the letter M (Maria).
Chair of Space Technology, Technische Universität Berlin, Marchstraße 12-14, 10587 Berlin, Germany

new_values.quote: FeOa  0.40 0.01 0.82 0.01 0.57 0.01 9.19 0.06 10.10 0.08 10.23 0.04 (FeO calculated from measured Fe2O3, conversion factor 0.8998)
Plagioclasea  37  32  31  (a: Plagioclase with high content in anorthite component; last column = mixed LX-M100)
Olivineb  9  16  15  (b: Olivine with high content of forsterite component)
The highest AP-cohesive strength was found for LX-T100 with 257.2 Pa, followed by LX-I50 with 214.3 Pa and LX-M100 with 185.2 Pa.

results.notes: Both listed local documents genuinely name LX-M100; no weak candidates in this simulant's group entry. Full XRD mineralogy (Table 3) and XRF oxide chemistry (Table 4) for the mixed LX-M100 product exist in the Part 1 paper (already in library_documents_naming_it) but the DB's oxides/minerals arrays are empty despite composition_status='withheld_unverified' — recommend the curator review whether this data should now be imported (quoted in full above as new_values). Library sweep (grep -rliw 'LX-M100'/'LXM100' over Sources_text) found no other document in the library naming this product beyond the two already listed. friction_angle=46.2 is sourced from Part 2 (not in the simulant's formal references list, added as NEW1) and is a 3-simulant AVERAGE, not LX-M100-specific — flagged in the value note. Part 2 also reports several other LX-M100-specific properties not attempted as new_values here due to uncertain DB field-name mapping: Hausner ratio 1.45±0.03 (Table 4, p.8), magnetic susceptibility χ=1.83e-5 emu/g (Table 7, p.11 — magnetite content 3-5 wt% noted qualitatively), BET specific surface area, oedometer compressibility index Cc, and visible/near-IR reflectance spectra (Fig.17, p.13-14).

values.quote: Since they occur as a mixture in most regions of the Moon's surface, the "intermediate" simulant TUBS-I was additionally introduced and investigated.
values.note: Inferred from the publication year of this 2022 paper, which is the introducing publication for TUBS-I; no explicit 'release date' statement exists.

No statement of TUBS-I's availability/production status was found in R161. Unlike TUBS-M/TUBS-T (for which the 2020 paper explicitly states they 'will be available for the space engineering and lunar science community'), TUBS-I is not mentioned in that context in either Linke paper. Since TUBS-I is produced on demand from the two base simulants, availability is plausible but not documented.

values.quote: Since they occur as a mixture in most regions of the Moon's surface, the "intermediate" simulant TUBS-I was additionally introduced and investigated. It consists of a 50:50 mixture of TUBS-M and TUBS-T.
values.note: CONTRADICTED, not merely unsupported: R161 explicitly defines TUBS-I as an 'intermediate' 50:50 mare+highland (TUBS-M + TUBS-T) blend, with mineralogical/chemical composition 'correspondingly average' of the two (Section 4.1: 'Note that TUBS-I is a 50:50 mixture of TUBS-M and TUBS-T, and the mineralogical and chemical composition is correspondingly average.'). The word 'ilmenite' occurs in R161 exactly once, in an unrelated sentence about a future chemically-adapted-simulant (CAS) additive mineral, never describing TUBS-I. This looks like a mislabeling in the database -- likely a confusion of 'TUBS-I' = Intermediate with 'ilmenite'. Recommend the curator change this field for S137, e.g. to 'Mare/Highland (Intermediate, 50:50 TUBS-M:TUBS-T)'.

values.quote: Institute for Particle Technology, TU Braunschweig, Volkmaroder Str. 5, 38104 Braunschweig, Germany ... The prefix "TUBS" stands for Technical University of Braunschweig.

results.notes: MOST IMPORTANT FINDING: the stored lunar_sample_reference 'Ilmenite-rich' for TUBS-I is contradicted by its own defining reference (R161), which describes TUBS-I as a straight 50:50 mixture of the mare (TUBS-M) and highland (TUBS-T) base simulants, with no ilmenite enrichment mentioned anywhere. This should be corrected by a curator. availability could not be sourced for TUBS-I specifically (see value note). No independent oxide/mineral composition table exists for TUBS-I: R161 states its chemistry is simply the arithmetic average of TUBS-M and TUBS-T (not separately measured), so no oxide/mineral new_values are reported here -- if the curator wants TUBS-I oxide numbers, they would need to be computed from the S069/S070 oxide values just reported (average of the two), which is a derived/curator decision, not something a document states outright. Two other library documents cite this Windisch et al. 2022 TUBS-I paper only in their own bibliography/related-work lists (ResearchGate-style 'View' citation or reference-list entry), without characterizing TUBS-I themselves, so were not opened as primary sources: Sources_text/papers/LRS/DIRT project/files/1763/388423686_Influence_of_loading_conditions_on_mechanical_behaviors_of_lunar_regolith_simulant_WH.html.txt and Sources_text/papers/LRS/1-s2.0-S0032063325001564-main.pdf.txt. Sources_text/papers/LRS/DIRT project/files/1643/S2095268624001381.html.txt (review, 'Research progress on the adaptability of lunar regolith simulant-based composites...') tabulates TUBS-I in two places: a mineral-type table ('TUBS-M 100% [Basalt]' / 'TUBS-T 100% [Anorthosite]' style categorical entries, not wt% composition) and a processing-comparison table giving a slightly different particle size ('TUBS-I d_m=87') than Table 2's 88.6 µm -- treated as a lower-confidence secondary citation and not used to override R161's own Table 2 value.

problems: Opened papers/Linke_etal_2020_TUBS-M_TUBS-T_modular_Regolith_Simulant_System_PlanetSpaceSci_180_104747.pdf. Title 'TUBS-M and TUBS-T based modular Regolith Simulant System for the support of lunar ISRU activities' and abstract 'The TUBS-M and TUBS-T simulants are based on basaltic and anorthositic bedrock, respectively.' are verbatim on p.1.
The local copy is the Elsevier 'Corrected proof' / ARTICLE IN PRESS version (pdfinfo; header 'Planetary and Space Science xxx (xxxx) xxx'). Page numbers 1-9 are proof pages, not final journal pages.
R054 and R055 are duplicate reference records for the same DOI 10.1016/j.pss.2019.104747. Both have local_path null although the PDF is in the library.

The quote is verbatim in Section 1.5 of papers/agent-fetched/Linke_etal_2022_...PMC9737658.html: 'the mare simulant TUBS-M and the terrae simulant TUBS-T. The prefix “TUBS” stands for Technical University of Braunschweig.'
NEW1 is not a new document. It has the same DOI (10.3390/ma15238561) as existing reference R161, already linked to S137. The curator should link R161 to S069 rather than create a new reference.

The author list is incomplete. The page lists Lisa Windisch, Stefan Linke, Magnus Jütte, Julian Baasch, Arno Kwade, Enrico Stoll and Carsten Schilde; the extractor omitted Baasch, Kwade and Stoll. The first author is Windisch, although the file name says 'Linke_etal'.
R054 Table 5, p.8: 'Bulk density ρB 1.41 g/cm3 [TUBS-M] 1.18 g/cm3 [TUBS-T]'. Checked on the rendered page image.
Corroborated by R161 Table A4, TUBS-M row '1.41 1.55 1.55 1.61 1.62' (3 kPa column = 1.41), and by R161 Table 2 bulk density '1.41–1.62'.
R161 (=NEW1) Table A3, 'Cohesion values of TUBS-M, TUBS-T, and TUBS-I at different shear stresses', TUBS-M row: '349.67 604.67 668.67 1023.67 1902.67' (Pa at 3/6/9/15/25 kPa). 349.67 Pa ≈ 0.35 kPa.
The caption and column headers call these 'shear stresses' (3 kPa ... 25 kPa), not 'preload' or 'consolidation' as the extractor says.
This conflicts with the listed reference R054, whose Table 5, p.8 gives 'Cohesion 0.6 kPa' for TUBS-M. The stored value should cite R161, not R054, and the 3 kPa condition should be recorded.

R054 Table 5, p.8: 'Solids density ρ 2.96 g/cm3'. The field is specific_gravity, while the paper gives solids density in g/cm3; the Methods (p.4) say it 'was determined by the supplier of the raw material and taken from the data sheet', so this is not the authors' own measurement.
R161 Table 2, x50 row: '76.7 [TUBS-M] 88.6 [TUBS-I] 96.0 [TUBS-T] 41–130 [lunar]'. Verified.

R054 Table 5, p.8 gives 'Median 87 μm' for TUBS-M, which conflicts. The extractor calls R054's number a 'different (laser-diffraction ...) measurement', but that does not tell the two apart: both papers used laser diffraction (Mastersizer 3000, dry unit Aero S). The field must cite R161, not R054.

The abstract quote exists verbatim in R161: '( x 50 = 76.7 to 96.0 µm)'. It is the combined x50 range of all three simulants; Section 4.6 says 'The x 50 of the three simulants ranges from 76.7 to 96.0 µm (see Table 2 )'. No document states it as TUBS-M's own distribution, so it fails the exact-product rule.
A TUBS-M-specific distribution does exist in R161 Table 2: x10 8.5, x50 76.7, x90 593.6 µm. The curator should replace the stored string with these.

The quote is verbatim in R054 Section 5 Conclusions, p.8: 'Within early 2020, the upscaling of the production of the basic simulants TUBS-M and TUBS-T as well as the preparation of corresponding data sheets ... will be completed.' It is a forecast about upscaling, not a statement of release.

The same paper says the base simulants were already done and in production in 2019. Section 3.1: 'The development of the two base simulants TUBS-M and TUBS-T (1) has been completed and these are currently being produced in larger quantities'. Section 4, p.7: 'Large quantity production ... will be started in 2019'.

Earlier dates exist. R161 reference 1 is Linke et al., 'TUBS-M and TUBS-T—New Lunar Regolith Simulant adaptable to local Lunar surface characteristics', 69th IAC, Bremen, 1–5 October 2018. The IGG-01 paper's table (files/1757) lists 'TUBS-M Germany 2018 Basalt Mare general use'. So 2020 is an interpretation, not a documented value.

Wrong location: the quote 'Large quantity production in the scale of several hundred kilograms of TUBS-M and TUBS-T will be started in 2019 and will be available for the space engineering and lunar science community.' is in Section 4 'Outlook and discussion', p.7, not Section 3.1. It is also a future-tense plan.

Stronger present-tense support is in a document the extractor did not cite for TUBS-M: Patzwald et al. 2025, Acta Astronautica 231, p.204 (Sources_text/papers/LRS/1-s2.0-S0094576525001109-main.pdf.txt), 'TUBS-M and TUBS-T are currently available, but the CAS and PAS variants are not.' Co-authors include Linke and Stoll.
'(Research)' is not stated in any document; the curator should decide whether to keep it.
R054 Section 5, p.8: 'TUBS-M (a maria-type simulant)'. Also Patzwald 2025, p.204: 'base simulants TUBS-M (Mare) and TUBS-T (Highland)'.
The R054 p.1 affiliation is verbatim, including the typo 'Brauschweig'.
R054 Table 2, p.7, TUBS-M Analysis column: 48.61, err 0.29. Checked on the rendered page.

Table 2, p.7: 2.29, err 0.02. Note that R161 Section 4.1 says TUBS-M's minor components 'such as TiO 2 , MnO, and Cr 2 O 3 , the measured values are in the low range (<1%)', which is inconsistent with 2.29 wt%. Curator flag.
Table 2, p.7: 0.04, err na.

problems: Same PDF and same verbatim title and abstract as R054. R055 duplicates R054 (same DOI). The local copy is the corrected-proof version.
The quote is verbatim in R161 Section 1.5 and names TUBS-T.
NEW1 is the same document as existing R161 (DOI 10.3390/ma15238561); the curator should link R161, not create a new reference.
The author list is incomplete (Baasch, Kwade and Stoll are missing).
R161 Table A4, 'Bulk densities of TUBS-M, TUBS-T, and TUBS-I at different shear stresses', TUBS-T row: '1.33 1.38 1.42 1.46 1.50'. The 3 kPa value is 1.33; R161 Table 2 also gives '1.33–1.46'.

R161 Table 2: x50 96.0 µm for TUBS-T. R055 Table 5 'Median 87 μm' conflicts; cite R161.

As for S069: the Conclusions quote (p.8) is a forecast, not a release date. The paper says development was completed and production underway in 2019. R161 reference 1 shows TUBS-T was presented at the 69th IAC, Bremen, October 2018, and the IGG-01 table lists 'TUBS-T Germany 2018 Anorthosite Highland'.
Wrong location: the quote is in Section 4 'Outlook and discussion', p.7, not Section 3.1. It is future tense.

The extractor gave the Patzwald 2025 page as 'not determined precisely'. It is Acta Astronautica 231, p.204, Section 1: 'TUBS-M and TUBS-T are currently available, but the CAS and PAS variants are not.' That paper is a research paper on the LX system, not a review.
The ESRIC directory (files/1735/simulants.html.txt) states 'Name TUBS-T Description Highlands (general) Availability Currently available Supplier/Contact Technische Universität Braunschweig Germany'.

A caveat the curator should see: the JLU-H paper (files/1756/S0032063322001489) says 'Some simulants, such as NAO-1 and TUBS-T, cannot be produced in large quantities due to the remote origin of their raw materials'.

R055 p.8: 'TUBS-T (a terrae-type simulant)'. R055 p.7: 'Each of the base simulant represents a typical maria (lunar lowlands) or terrae (lunar highlands) simulant'. Also ISECG Table 9 lists 'TUBS-T ... Highlands (general)'.

problems: The title and Section 1.5 quote 'the “intermediate” simulant TUBS-I was additionally introduced and investigated. It consists of a 50:50 mixture of TUBS-M and TUBS-T.' are verbatim in papers/agent-fetched/Linke_etal_2022_...PMC9737658.html. local_path is null in the group file although the file is in the library.
R161 Table A4, TUBS-I row: '1.43 1.49 1.51 1.56 1.58'. The 3 kPa value is 1.43; Table 2 gives '1.43–1.56'. The stored value should record the 3 kPa shear-stress condition.

R161 Table 2: x50 88.6 µm for TUBS-I. The value is correct, but the extractor's note is wrong. The 1643 review's 'TUBS-I d m =87' cites reference [131], which is B. Reitz et al., 'Additive manufacturing under lunar gravity and microgravity', Microgravity Sci Technol 33 (2021) 25, not the 2022 paper. Reitz et al. in turn state 'average grain size of 87 µm Linke et al. (2020)', a figure carried over from the 2020 paper's TUBS-M/T median.
R161 contains no release date, and the quoted Section 1.5 sentence contains no year. The extractor's premise that R161 is 'the introducing publication for TUBS-I' is false.

TUBS-I was already used and characterised in Reitz et al. 2021 (received 19 November 2020, published online 24 March 2021; co-authors Linke and Stoll). I fetched it and saved it at Sources/papers/agent-fetched/Reitz_etal_2021_Additive_Manufacturing_Under_Lunar_Gravity_and_Microgravity_MicrogravSciTechnol_33_25_TUBS-I.pdf. p.7 reads: 'The regolith simulant variant TUBS-I is used for the experiments is described here.' So 2022 is not supported, and TUBS-I existed by 2020/2021.

I agree it is unsupported. No group document states TUBS-I availability. ESRIC lists only TUBS-T and TUBS-H. Patzwald 2025, p.204 names only TUBS-M and TUBS-T as 'currently available'. R054 says site-specific intermediate simulants are 'Mixed only on demand from TUBS-M and TUBS-T', but does not name TUBS-I.

I agree 'Ilmenite-rich' is unsupported and contradicted. R161 contains 'ilmenite' only once, in the CAS sentence ('CAS additionally contain different proportions of minerals found in lunar rocks like ilmenite or olivine'). R161 Section 4.1 says 'TUBS-I is a 50:50 mixture of TUBS-M and TUBS-T, and the mineralogical and chemical composition is correspondingly average.'

Further contradicted by Reitz et al. 2021, p.7: 'TUBS-I combines maria and terrae properties and therefore is a chemical and mineralogical mix of mainly basalt and anorthosite'. Its Table 2 gives TiO2 of only 1.2 wt%.

R161 affiliation 'Institute for Particle Technology, TU Braunschweig, Volkmaroder Str. 5, 38104 Braunschweig, Germany' and Section 1.5 'The prefix “TUBS” stands for Technical University of Braunschweig.' are verbatim.

Reitz, Lotz, Gerdes, Linke, Olsen, Pflieger, Sohrt, Ernst, Taschner, Neumann, Stoll and Overmeyer (2021), 'Additive Manufacturing Under Lunar Gravity and Microgravity', Microgravity Sci. Technol. 33:25, doi 10.1007/s12217-021-09878-4, CC BY. It is not in the library; I fetched it and saved it at Sources/papers/agent-fetched/Reitz_etal_2021_Additive_Manufacturing_Under_Lunar_Gravity_and_Microgravity_MicrogravSciTechnol_33_25_TUBS-I.pdf. It refutes the extractor's claim that 'No independent oxide/mineral composition table exists for TUBS-I'. Table 2, p.7, 'Average oxidic composition of the maria and terrae regolith Taylor (1975) compared to TUBS-I', TUBS-I in wt%: SiO2 48.7, TiO2 1.2, FeO 5.6, MgO 4.7, CaO 11.4, Na2O 3.4 (no Al2O3 given). These match the arithmetic mean of the R054 and R055 analyses, so they are probably computed rather than measured, but the document states them for TUBS-I. p.8 gives 'the known solid density ρ R of the regolith simulant of 2.84 g/cm3', a candidate specific_gravity for TUBS-I (≈ mean of 2.96 and 2.71). R161 Table 2 also gives TUBS-I x10 5.5, x50 88.6, x90 1074.9 µm, tapped density 1.65 g/cm3, average Hausner ratio 1.10 and aspect ratio 0.50-0.68. results.notes: S014's own listed reference R014 could not be opened at all. All supporting evidence instead comes from six documents found through the library sweep (none of which were already in S014's 'references' list, so all are reported as new_references). Two independent-looking sources give MUTUALLY CONTRADICTORY full oxide tables for DNA-1: Kjøniksen et al. 2021 (NEW2, corroborated word-for-word by Zhou et al. 2021's Table 4, NEW5 - both give SiO2 47.79, Al2O3 19.16, Fe2O3/FeO 8.75, CaO 8.28, K2O 3.52, Na2O 4.38, MgO 1.86, TiO2 1.00) versus Sandeep et al. 2019's Table 1, which reports what it calls Cesaretti et al. (2014)'s numbers for DNA-1 (SiO2 41.90, Al2O3 16.02, Fe2O3 14.60, CaO 12.90, Na2O 2.66, K2O 2.53, MgO 6.34, TiO2 1.31) - these differ substantially on every oxide, most starkly Fe2O3 (8.75 vs 14.60) and MgO (1.86 vs 6.34). This directly explains why the DB's composition_status for DNA-1 is 'withheld_unverified' and both sets are reported as new_values for a curator to adjudicate rather than picking one. Ceccanti et al. 2010 (NEW1), the earliest paper found defining 'D-NA-1' and confirming the Monolite/ESA institution, contains its own JSC-1A vs D-NA-1 vs Apollo chemical comparison but only as a bar chart (Fig. 4); its numbers were not machine-readable as text and were not extracted (would require rendering the page as an image, not done here). release_date=2014 could not be grounded: the earliest opened primary document is from 2010, and R014 (probably the source of '2014') was inaccessible. A ResearchGate-saved page for an unrelated 2012 TJ-1 paper (papers/LRS/DIRT project/files/1765/276962935_Properties_of_TJ-1_Lunar_Soil_Simulant.html) contains a stray table row 'DNA-1 [48] Mare, Low-Ti General 2014' that plausibly is the ultimate source of both release_date=2014 and lunar_sample_reference='Low-Ti Mare', but it is embedded in that page's 'Citations (88)' sidebar of snippets from other citing papers, so its true source paper could not be identified with confidence and it was not used as a citable reference. Liu et al. 2024 (NEW3)'s own comparison table elsewhere lists 'DNA-1A' with country 'Australia', which conflicts with the known Italian/Onano origin (Sandeep 2019, Marzulli & Cafaro 2019) - flagged as a likely compilation error in that review, not used for anything. Two Liu et al. 2024 (NEW3) process-parameter tables also show DNA-1 rows for sintered/geopolymer composites (a sieved fraction 'd=25-1000' for an electron-beam sintering test, and NaOH/regolith ratios 0.32-0.45 for a geopolymer test, both citing other numbered references not opened here) - these describe processed-composite test conditions rather than the base simulant's own specification, so they were not mapped to any stored or new field. Passing-mention-only documents found in the library sweep but not opened in depth: papers/LRS/s41598-023-50391-y.pdf.txt (lists 'DNA' among many simulants in one citation-superscript list, no data).

checks.notes:
Main correction: lunar_sample_reference 'Apollo 14' is supported, and the extractor missed it. The support is PolyU-1 (papers/LRS/1-s2.0-S2095268624001150-main.pdf) p.2 / journal p.1318: 'A low-Ti mare simulant TJ-1 was created from red volcanic ash deposits collected in northern China to match the physical and mechanical properties of Apollo 14 samples [19].'

The stored cohesion 1.0 matches the CAS-1 row directly above TJ-1 in CUMT-1 Table 4 ('CAS-1 1.00 33.30'), so it is probably a row-slip error.

Source material conflicts across documents:
- R049 abstract: 'red volcanic ash deposits collected from northern China'.
- CUMT-1 p.4: TJ-1 is among simulants 'manufactured based on the basaltic volcanic scoria mined from the Changbai Mountains'.
- LX p.203: 'basalt slag from the same source as CAS-1'.

The library sweep (grep -w TJ-1, TJ1, Tongji-1, Tongji) found two passing mentions the extractor did not list:
- papers/Zhou_etal_2021_BH-1_lunar_soil_simulant_geopolymer_Engineering_7_1631-1645.pdf: 'Chinese Academy of Sciences (CAS)-1, and Tongji (TJ)-1 [15]'. The spelling '(TJ)-1' escapes a TJ-1 word grep.
- papers/LRS/DIRT project/files/1643/S2095268624001381.html (Liu et al. 2024 review). Its mineral table row 'TJ-1/2 > 30 √ √ √' is a combined TJ-1/TJ-2 row and cannot be used for either product. Its row 'TJ-1 d <45 SH+SS′ 0.26–0.3 AH 60 3–28 4.3–58.8 [143]' describes a TJ-1-based geopolymer from [143] = Xiong et al., Constr Build Mater, not properties of the simulant itself.

The Engelschiøn 2020 mention ('JSC-1A, JSC-2A, TJ-1, MLS and DNA are alkali-rich basalts and basanites') is a passing mention. Its density numbers (2.90 etc.) are for EAC-1, JSC-1A, JSC-2A, DNA and NU-LHT-3M, not TJ-1.

The R049 RG page has many citing-work excerpts naming TJ-1. None of them gives 1.55, 2.9 or 1.0 kPa for TJ-1.

No TJ-1 primary data sheet or full text exists in Sources or papers/agent-fetched; grep of agent-fetched PDFs and HTML found no TJ-1, TJ-2 or Tongji. The 'Zou_etal_2024' and 'Li et al. - 2022' copies are text-identical duplicates of NEW2 and NEW1.

checks.notes:
Library sweep for TJ-2 (grep -w TJ-2 and TJ2) found only the 8 documents already listed. All are inventory or list mentions paired with TJ-1, with no TJ-2-specific numbers.

The NEU-1 and TJ-1 RG pages share one citing excerpt, which appears to come from Corazzari et al. 2021, 'History and Future Perspectives for the Evaluation of the Toxicity of Celestial Dust'. If the curator wants that excerpt as evidence, the chapter itself should be obtained and cited, not Li 2019 or Jiang 2012.

The Liu et al. 2024 review (papers/LRS/DIRT project/files/1643/S2095268624001381.html) lists 'TJ-1/2 [49]', where [49] = Jiang, Li, Sun 2012 (TJ-1 paper). Its mineral row 'TJ-1/2 > 30 √ √ √' is combined and cannot be used for TJ-2. The extractor did not list it for TJ-2.

The likely primary source, Jiang, Li, Wang, Zhang 2010, 'A new lunar soil simulant in China', Earth and Space 2010 pp. 3617-3623, is not in Sources or papers/agent-fetched.

I agree with the extractor's metadata flag: library_documents_naming_it_total is 0 even though 6 documents are listed.
